newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish private bond trading up 2 pct through June.
newsitem.headline: Spanish private bond trading up 2 pct through June.

text.p: Spain's main market of private bonds, run by the Association of Dealers in Financial Assets (AIAF), had a trading volume of 1.478 trillion pesetas in the first half of 1997, up two percent from a year earlier.
Of this total, 735 billion pesetas were done in note and bonds, 314 billion in matador, 297 billion in promissory bills and 134 billion in mortgage bonds.

Banco Bilbao Vizcaya (BBV) was the most active dealer trading 252 billion pesetas in the first six months of the year. It was followed by Spanish saving banks association CECA which traded 203 billion pesetas.
Banco Exterior was rated third with 179 billion pesetas.
Deutsche Bank was leader in the trading of Matadores.
